turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Starting spindle diagnostic procedure.

ground_truth.node_text: Start

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Begin with a warm-up run. Bring the spindle up to fifty percent speed and let it run for ten minutes.

ground_truth.node_text: Warm up run, spindle at 50% speed for 10 minutes

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Warm-up complete, spindle has been running at fifty percent for ten minutes.

ground_truth.node_text: Warm up run, spindle at 50% speed for 10 minutes

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Mount a calibrated accelerometer on the front bearing housing using either a flat washer stud or magnetic base. Run the spindle at three thousand RPM with no toolholder fitted and record the RMS vibration velocity in millimeters per second. Then repeat the measurement at maximum rated speed and compare both readings against the ISO 10816 zone limits for this machine class.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a calibrated accelerometer on the front bearing housing with a flat washer stud or magnetic base. Run the spindle at 3000 revolutions per minute with no toolholder fitted and record the root mean square vibration velocity in millimetres per second. Repeat at the maximum rated speed and compare both readings against the ISO 10816 zone limits for this machine class.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Accelerometer mounted and measurements taken. At three thousand RPM I'm reading one point four millimeters per second, and at max speed two point one millimeters per second. Both are within the ISO zone limits.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a calibrated accelerometer on the front bearing housing with a flat washer stud or magnetic base. Run the spindle at 3000 revolutions per minute with no toolholder fitted and record the root mean square vibration velocity in millimetres per second. Repeat at the maximum rated speed and compare both readings against the ISO 10816 zone limits for this machine class.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the vibration level below the alarm limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Vibration level below alarm limit?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The vibration is within limits, but I'm hearing a rhythmic knocking sound coming from the bearing housing that wasn't there before.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, both readings are well below the alarm threshold.

ground_truth.node_text: Vibration level below alarm limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the bearing temperature within the rated operating limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Bearing temperature within rated operating limit?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the front bearing is at fifty-eight degrees and the rear at sixty-two degrees Celsius. Both are within spec with temperature rise of twenty degrees above ambient.

ground_truth.node_text: Bearing temperature within rated operating limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the radial runout within two micrometer tolerance?

ground_truth.node_text: Radial runout within 2 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, I'm seeing one point six micrometers total indicator reading on the spindle nose taper. That's within the two micrometer limit.

ground_truth.node_text: Radial runout within 2 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the axial play within three micrometer tolerance?

ground_truth.node_text: Axial play within 3 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, I'm averaging four point two micrometers of axial deflection across three measurements. That's over the three micrometer limit.

ground_truth.node_text: Axial play within 3 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the preload spacer or shim to reduce the axial play.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pre load spacer or shim to reduce axial play

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I'm seeing metal shavings in the bearing housing and the inner race looks scored. Should I be concerned about bearing damage before I adjust the preload?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Preload spacer adjusted, I've installed a thinner shim to tighten up the axial clearance.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pre load spacer or shim to reduce axial play

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Apply a thin even coat of engineer's blue to a clean test arbor with the correct taper angle. Insert the arbor, rotate by hand under moderate axial load, then withdraw and inspect the contact pattern. You're looking for uniform blue transfer over at least seventy percent of the taper length.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply a thin even coat of engineer's blue to a clean test arbor with the correct taper angle for this spindle. Insert the arbor, rotate by hand under moderate axial load, then withdraw and inspect the contact pattern. The blue should transfer uniformly over at least 70% of the taper length; a spotted or narrow band pattern indicates taper bore damage or swarf contamination.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Test arbor inserted and rotated. I'm seeing good blue transfer across about eighty percent of the taper length, nice and uniform.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply a thin even coat of engineer's blue to a clean test arbor with the correct taper angle for this spindle. Insert the arbor, rotate by hand under moderate axial load, then withdraw and inspect the contact pattern. The blue should transfer uniformly over at least 70% of the taper length; a spotted or narrow band pattern indicates taper bore damage or swarf contamination.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the taper contact pattern above eighty-five percent bearing area?

ground_truth.node_text: Taper contact pattern above 85% bearing area?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Hey, before we continue, do you know if the new safety harnesses came in yet? I need to grab one before the shift ends.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the contact pattern is around eighty percent. It's close but not quite at the eighty-five percent target.

ground_truth.node_text: Taper contact pattern above 85% bearing area?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Clean and reinspect the taper, and check for any signs of fretting.

ground_truth.node_text: Clean and reinspect taper, check for fretting

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I cleaned the taper and checked for fretting like you said, but I'm noticing some discoloration and heat marks around the bearing seat that don't look like fretting—looks more like thermal damage.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Taper cleaned thoroughly with solvent and reinspected. No fretting visible, surfaces look good.

ground_truth.node_text: Clean and reinspect taper, check for fretting

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Connect the calibrated pull stud extraction dynamometer to the toolholder retention knob. Apply a steady pull along the spindle axis and record the peak force at which the drawbar releases the toolholder. Compare the result against the minimum drawbar force in the maintenance specification.

ground_truth.node_text: Connect the calibrated pull stud extraction dynamometer to the toolholder retention knob. Apply a steady pull along the spindle axis and record the peak force at which the drawbar releases the toolholder. Compare the result against the minimum drawbar force listed in the spindle maintenance specification; a low reading indicates disc spring wear or stacking loss.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I'm seeing hydraulic fluid leaking from the drawbar cylinder seal while I'm setting this up — there's a small puddle forming under the spindle housing.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Dynamometer connected and test complete. The drawbar released at eight hundred and fifty newtons peak force.

ground_truth.node_text: Connect the calibrated pull stud extraction dynamometer to the toolholder retention knob. Apply a steady pull along the spindle axis and record the peak force at which the drawbar releases the toolholder. Compare the result against the minimum drawbar force listed in the spindle maintenance specification; a low reading indicates disc spring wear or stacking loss.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the drawbar retention force within the rated range?

ground_truth.node_text: Drawbar retention force within rated range?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the spec calls for a minimum of one thousand newtons. Eight fifty is below the acceptable range.

ground_truth.node_text: Drawbar retention force within rated range?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the drawbar spring stack or replace the disc springs.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust drawbar spring stack or replace disc springs

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've replaced two worn disc springs in the stack and reassembled the drawbar assembly.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust drawbar spring stack or replace disc springs

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Mount a dial test indicator against the reference artifact clamped in the spindle at cold start. Zero the indicator and allow the spindle to run at operating speed for thirty minutes. Record the indicator displacement at ten minute intervals and note the total thermal growth at stabilization, then compare against the stored compensation value.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a dial test indicator against the reference artefact clamped in the spindle at cold start. Zero the indicator and allow the spindle to run at operating speed for 30 minutes. Record the indicator displacement at 10 minute intervals and note the total thermal growth value at stabilisation; compare against the growth compensation value stored in the machine thermal compensation table.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Thermal growth test complete. I recorded twelve micrometers at ten minutes, eighteen at twenty minutes, and twenty-two micrometers at thirty minutes where it stabilized. That matches the compensation table value of twenty-two micrometers.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a dial test indicator against the reference artefact clamped in the spindle at cold start. Zero the indicator and allow the spindle to run at operating speed for 30 minutes. Record the indicator displacement at 10 minute intervals and note the total thermal growth value at stabilisation; compare against the growth compensation value stored in the machine thermal compensation table.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the thermal growth within the compensation model tolerance?

ground_truth.node_text: Thermal growth within compensation model tolerance?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the measured growth matches the model prediction within tolerance.

ground_truth.node_text: Thermal growth within compensation model tolerance?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the spindle speed within plus or minus zero point one percent at all test speeds?

ground_truth.node_text: Spindle speed within ±0.1% at all test speeds?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, I'm seeing a zero point two percent error at the high test speed. The tachometer reads three thousand twelve RPM when commanded three thousand.

ground_truth.node_text: Spindle speed within ±0.1% at all test speeds?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the speed reference gain in the drive parameter.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust speed reference gain in drive parameter

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Hey, before I do that, do you know where the updated lockout-tagout procedures are posted? I can't find the new version on the board.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Speed reference gain adjusted in the drive controller. The calibration should be corrected now.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust speed reference gain in drive parameter

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Run the spindle at maximum rated speed with the normal toolholder fitted for five minutes. Record the vibration velocity with the accelerometer on the front bearing housing and compare against the baseline measurement from the most recent full service.

ground_truth.node_text: Run the spindle at maximum rated speed with the normal toolholder fitted for five minutes. Record vibration velocity with the accelerometer on the front bearing housing and compare against the baseline vibration measurement taken at the same speed during the most recent full service. An increase of more than 30% above baseline requires bearing assessment before releasing the spindle to production.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Final vibration test complete at max speed with toolholder. I'm reading two point three millimeters per second, which is only fifteen percent above the baseline of two point zero.

ground_truth.node_text: Run the spindle at maximum rated speed with the normal toolholder fitted for five minutes. Record vibration velocity with the accelerometer on the front bearing housing and compare against the baseline vibration measurement taken at the same speed during the most recent full service. An increase of more than 30% above baseline requires bearing assessment before releasing the spindle to production.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the final vibration within the warning limit at full speed?

ground_truth.node_text: Final vibration within warning limit at full speed?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, it's well within limits. The increase is only fifteen percent, far below the thirty percent warning threshold.

ground_truth.node_text: Final vibration within warning limit at full speed?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Log all measurements and update the spindle maintenance record.

ground_truth.node_text: Log all measurements and update spindle maintenance record

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: All measurements logged and maintenance record updated in the system.

ground_truth.node_text: Log all measurements and update spindle maintenance record

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Procedure complete. The spindle has passed all diagnostic checks and is cleared for production use. Document the completed procedure in the shift log.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Procedure complete

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Understood, I'll document the clearance in the shift log.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Procedure complete
